confirmed.title: Both entropy lines (acceptance <= 0.06, RL stop line 0.3 over 5 updates) average over every answer token, so for G they would mostly measure coordinate digits
confirmed.where: evaluation.py:519-534 (entropy over all generated positions up to '</action>'), :401-402 (only the per-answer mean is stored), :597-605; q3dev accept_summary.py:33/63/80-81; ray_trainer.py:2610-2617 (actor/entropy is a token mean); train_chain.py:401-407; G.yaml sft.select (l.27) and rl.guards (l.41); PREREG note 6, applied unchanged by PREREG_G_vs_D_draft §1.
confirmed.what: Over all 23,719 P2t labels: 28.99 tokens per answer = 17.33 targets + 11.66 action (the action part equals D's). That includes 6.50 one-digit tokens (22.4%) and 2.18 coordinates. Units and tens digits are uniform (2.30 nats), and one unit is 0.256 px. Budget: D e9 spends 0.238 nats per answer, so to stay under 0.06 the targets segment can carry about 1.42 nats (about 1.1 at Cr e7 / D_noP0 e7), i.e. at most about 0.2 nats per digit. Calibrated coordinates (sd 2-20 units, T 0.8) give 0.17-0.35, 3-6x the line. Collapsed digits dilute action entropy about 2.7x: C e4's 0.106 would read 0.039 and pass. Either way pass/fail tracks digit sharpness, not the action policy. 'Every epoch fails' is likely but not certain: action-only cells sharpened 4-9x over 10 epochs, and the main line's statement start reached 0.009. Per-segment entropy is not stored, so changing the rule later means re-running the acceptance (about 7 card-hours) after seeing G's numbers, which the draft forbids once finalised. RL guard: under the current acceptance a passing epoch starts RL at 1.0-1.2x its acceptance value, so an immediate stop is unlikely (the code-dimension finding was refuted on this). But if the acceptance moves to the action segment and the guard does not, digit-heavy starts of about 0.1-0.35 can reach 0.3. Dilution also makes the line about 2.4x less sensitive to action drift: E-old's stop at 0.42 would read about 0.2.
confirmed.fix: Ask the user and write the rule into PREREG_G_vs_D before launch. (1) G's acceptance entropy is the token-weighted mean over the action segment only, from the token reaching '<action>' (always the merged '><' in G) through '</action>'. Keep the same 0.06 and 1% lines, and report whole-answer and targets entropy (also per digit) with no line. (2) G's RL guard reads the same action-segment entropy: log actor/entropy_action and actor/entropy_targets from per-turn targets spans in the agent loop and set guards.entropy_key. Alternatively, fix a G line before RL from the picked epoch's measured split. The two lines must move together. Code, about 25 lines plus a CPU test: VllmPolicy.generate keeps per-position entropies, splits them using Logprob.decoded_token, and stores entropy_action/tokens_action/entropy_targets/tokens_targets. The split was tested: pieces rejoin 23,719/23,719 for G and D, and D's measure is unchanged (11.661-token action segment). Add a matrix-side accept_summary that judges entropy_action (q3dev's copy reads only entropy/tokens), and have m3_cells use it for G. Land this before G's SFT plan is written or after its sft_eval, and before the acceptance chain starts. Land the RL span logging (about 40 lines plus tests) before G's RL plan.

confirmed.title: The per-turn pointing reward pays more for more, shorter turns
confirmed.where: env.py:1198-1202 (+0.1 x score per turn); max_episode_steps 12 counts primitive actions and max_turns is 12; reward_score is the sum of the env rewards.
confirmed.what: The mechanism is confirmed: at most 1.2 per episode against a success reward of 5.0, already noted at PREREG draft l.101. Its size is smaller than claimed: switching to one action per turn would add about 2.5 turns to a failed D episode and about 1.6 to a successful one, i.e. +0.16-0.25 at a perfect score, not +0.4. disputed.title: System prompt shows a two-slot format and example (A and B) for one-object families
disputed.why_disputed: The facts are agreed. prompt.py:237 and _response_format use 2 slots. 3,662 of 9,075 P2t rows (7,474 turns) belong to one-object families and have 1-slot user blocks and labels under this text. An answer 'A: ..; B: none' on a one-slot task is a letters error and scores 0. One p2t skeptic rated it minor and now-or-never: RL must show the SFT's text, and FORMAT_DRIFT_R12 shows RL copying placeholders from format examples; any fix should key on task_type, not current_item. The other p2t skeptic and both code skeptics called it harmless: the design is deliberate and documented (CHANGES 8.1, pinned by test_system_prompt); the description defers to the per-turn format block; the SFT trains only 1-slot answers for these families; SFT/RL/eval text is identical (9,375/9,375); a slip still executes its action and loses at most 0.1. A fix would mean regenerating P2t and sft_trajectories right before launch. The evidence of harm is thin.
